status: authored 2026-10-03; generated into the world-local pack cobblers_markets by tools/markets.py; keepers placed by tools/reapply.py R17M; NOT run in game (docs/mechanics/MARKET_GATING.md section 5 is the experiment)
owner_brief: the owner, 2026-10-03: 'I want a player to rely on money throughout the game, and to advance materially as they travel ... Backpack tiers from the Cobbleverse backpack mod, unlocked town by town so a player upgrades as they go ... Per-town stock that reads as the place - a mining town sells what a mining town would. Priced so money matters.'

mechanism.summary: a market keeper is a Cobblemon dialogue NPC beside the town's Mart: one option per shelf item, an option gated on a badge visible only to a player holding that badge (compile_dialogue 'flag' probe -> isVisible), each option running a function that re-checks the gate, reads the balance, refuses if short, charges by macro, verifies the balance fell by exactly the price, and only then gives the item as the player. The ferry's sequence (tools/ferries.py trip_lines) with the teleport replaced by a give
sources: docs/mechanics/MARKET_GATING.md sections 4-5 (the recommendation and its experiment)
tools/compile_dialogue.py: visible_when -> isVisible; the flag probe; the function effect
tools/ferries.py trip_lines: cooldown, gate re-check, balance read (EXP-040), macro charge (EXP-042 run 1), verify
experiments/EXP-022-native-dialogue-runtime/README.md bugs 1-2: give runs as the player, and the score objective exists before a store
mechanism.rung: 5 (datapack) + 7 (functions), with 2 (CobbleDollars) for the money and 4 (configuration) for the recipes; no scripting layer, no companion, no mod
mechanism.what_it_is_not: the Mart clerks (data/traders.json) are untouched: they keep the trade GUI and the ungated basics. A town gets a clerk AND a keeper

income_basis.source: docs/mechanics/PROGRESSION_LADDER.md section 0.2 (model B, the middle bracket, at cobbleDollarsIncomeMultiplier 1.25 = docs/research/INCOME_MEASUREMENT.md section 2.4 x 2.5). Not measured here: EXP-A (U-2) collapses the band
income_basis.target_source: PROGRESSION_LADDER.md section 0.3: 'cumulative spend stays near 0.65-0.70 of cumulative income at every badge. The remaining 30-35% is the Mart, the ferry, the stones and the blackout.' The blackout is a flat $600 (data/blackout.json money.charge_rule)
income_basis.counts: the critical path only (the eight gym towns and Pallet), one of each option, a pick-one group at its dearest member, stretch items excluded from the ratio and included in the hard check that a badge's cumulative ask never exceeds its cumulative income

purchase.cooldown_why: the ferry's rule (data/ferries.json trip.cooldown_why): a second submit of the same option must not pay twice. The menu closes after every purchase, so one second is ample

messages.voice: PLACEHOLDERS for Codex's voice (the keepers' greetings are on the counters). Placeholders: {item}, {price}, {count}, {requirement}, and {balance} in 'short' only
messages.gated: I only sell that to trainers with {requirement}.
messages.charge_failed: The payment didn't go through, so nothing changed hands. Check your balance and try again.
messages.give_failed: I couldn't hand that over, so your ${price} is back with you.

stalls_basis.brief: the owner, 2026-10-03: 'More traders, and new ones. The backpack ladder landed last night -- build out the rest of the stock the same way, per town, reading as the place. Every town should have somewhere a player goes to spend money.' The survey is docs/world-building/TOWN_SQUARES_SURVEY.md
stalls_basis.why_this_pattern: a stall is a keeper on tools/markets.py's machinery (a dialogue menu and the purchase function whose charge macro EXP-042 proved), not a data/traders.json shopkeeper: a traders.json trader sells its BCA template's own trade list, filtered, so it cannot be told to sell a fishing town's rods or a stationer's paper without an authored CobbleMerchantShop, and that path (the Exchange's) is proof P-7, not run; it is also generated from the installed template, so it cannot be built or tested without a server. The keeper pattern can say exactly what each stall sells, gate a line if one ever needs it, and is placed by R17M with the counters
stalls_basis.budget: every line is an ungated `provision` (vanilla food, tools, rope, paper, fuel): not a rung on the ladder, so not counted by the curve, which stays the counters' (markets.py priced: a gated stall line on the critical path WOULD count). The money they take comes out of the 30-35% the curve leaves for the Mart, ferries, stones and the blackout (income_basis.target_source); each is something a player can also gather or craft, so it is a convenience bought with spare money, never a gate
stalls_basis.prices: above 2.5x data's bank sell-back for every food line (bank.json pays 5-20 for vanilla food; PROGRESSION_LADDER 0.5's multiplier reading), and set against the Mart's own scale (Poke Ball 200, Potion 200): a meal or a bundle of fuel for about one ball, a tool or instrument for two to five

stalls_basis.left_out: ids considered and left out of every stall: minecraft:cake (alcremie's neededNearbyBlocks), minecraft:rail (carkol and coalossal), minecraft:wheat_seeds (it places minecraft:wheat, beheeyem's): data/spawn_blocks.json names each, so a player who buys one decides encounters where they put it. cobblemon:poke_rod (verified in Cobblemon-fabric-1.8.0+1.21.1.jar) is withheld: it catches Pokemon, which stock_policy keeps off ungated stalls. Cobblecuisine teas and shakes are withheld: their boosts (shiny, catch rate, EVs; cobblecuisine.json boostSettings) are power, not provisions. stalls_basis.sites: a stall keeper stands where data/plaza_centres.json (the squares' contract, built in parallel) seats its `stall`; until that file exists, at the fallback measured from the data alone: inside the plan's plaza rect, 2-3 in from its edge (the middle is the centrepiece's), off the plaza's flush-lamp grid (tools/town_plan.py: every 27 from the corner) and its neighbours, 4.5+ from the waystone and every placed NPC and keeper, 3.5+ from every walked route point, turned to the square's centre. Integrated 2026-10-03 against the merged contract: every record names the contract stall whose theme fits its goods and carries that stall's theme word as `sells` (its own `stall_why` says why), and every contract stall is staffed once, by an existing keeper or one authored for it. The counter stands at stall 1 except at Tilpey (stall 4, `battle_items`: the counter's power stays behind its badge) and Steepside (stall 2, the contract's 'Tea House Kitchen'); Pallet's counter is on its one stall, `packs`. A new trader's fallback `at` is its contract seat, copied

stall_merchant.owner_brief: the owner, 2026-10-04, at Stoneford's square: 'the steve villagers aren't it, it should be the cobbleverse ones that have nice ui'
stall_merchant.source: docs/research/notes/cobbleverse-merchants.md sections 1-3: the entity, VillagerData and CobbleMerchantShop shape tools/traders.py already summons from the BCA shopkeeper templates; a merchant summoned on staging 2026-10-04 with an authored two-offer list held it and echoed it back with data get (the purchase through its screen is NOT yet observed)
stall_merchant.keeper: every sited stall's keeper is a CobbleDollars merchant at its seat (the squares' contract keeper_at, else the record's at/yaw), named keeper.name, NoAI, PersistenceRequired, Invulnerable, Silent, turned to the seat's yaw, tagged cobblers_stall and cobblers_stall_<id>; keeper.greeting is not shown (the merchant's screen has none) and is kept for the record
stall_merchant.offers: one CobbleMerchantShop category per stall, named by the stall's `category` (its theme in words); one offer per stock line, Item {count: 1, id: item}, Price the line's UNIT price as a string (price / count; a line whose price does not divide by its count is refused). The merchant screen sells singly with a quantity selector, and every offer in every BCA template and in the staging probe is count 1: what the screen does with Item.count above 1 is not verified (research note, Unknown), so 16 torches for $160 is offered as Torch at $10, sixteen for $160
stall_merchant.money: CobbleDollars' own screen takes the price from the buyer's balance; tools/markets.py emits no purchase function, dialogue or NPC class for a merchant stall, so nothing charges twice
stall_merchant.replaces: the Cobblemon dialogue keeper (spawnnpcat cobblers:npc_stall_<id>) R17M placed until 2026-10-04: once the new merchant stands, its place step kills every cobblemon:npc within remove_radius of its spot (the old keeper stood there, or one block behind it on today's table before the tents moved the keeper to the open front); every other placed NPC stands 3.5+ away (NPC_CLEAR)
stall_merchant.gated_lines: refused on a stall: the merchant shows one list to every player and cannot hide a line until a badge (MARKET_GATING.md section 1); a gated line belongs on a counter

decisions_pending.question: should the badge-gated counters also become CobbleDollars merchants?
decisions_pending.default_taken: no: the counters stay Cobblemon dialogue clerks. A merchant's CobbleMerchantShop is one list per entity, shown to every player (docs/research/notes/cobbleverse-merchants.md section 2, 'No per-player stock'), so it cannot hide a line until the player holds the badge; the counters' isVisible options can. No verified per-player mechanism was found: CobbleDollars 2.0.0+Beta-6's `/cm open shop <id>` might open a per-badge shop for one player from a dialogue option, but it is not installed and not tested (same note, section 4)

decisions_pending.question: every stall merchant also opens the global CobbleDollars bank on shift-right-click (sell-back of bank.json's list): acceptable?
decisions_pending.default_taken: accepted: the 14 Mart clerks already expose the same bank, so the stalls add places, not a capability (research note section 3). Denying it needs the permission cobbledollars.cobblemerchant.open.bank and a permissions mod, not checked
